verdict_reason: Explicitly requested seam reviewed: tests/integration/test_doctor_fix_lines_clear_their_finding.py executes production doctor fix lines via `subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", command], cwd=root, ...)`. Traced every substitution: the `Plant.substitutions` dicts that fill each fix line's `<placeholder>` tokens are dataclass literals hardcoded in the test module itself (fixed strings such as a release id, a document name, an audit slug chosen by the test author) — none is read from file content, external input, or anything an untrusted contributor could shape at review time; `_resolve()` asserts no `<` survives substitution, so a silently-unresolved placeholder cannot reach the shell. Every `subprocess.run` and the shared `_git()` helper pin `cwd=root`, where `root` is pytest's own `tmp_path` fixture (a fresh, isolated directory created and torn down per test) — no command in this module runs outside that fixture tree. The `_git()` helper additionally pins `env={"HOME": str(root), "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": "/dev/null"}`, so git commands cannot read the invoking user's global config. Cross-checked against production: `dadaia_workspace/features/specs/rules.py`'s `fix_help` strings are consumed exactly once at runtime, by `render_fix_help()` in `dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/doctor.py`, which only feeds `typer.Option(..., help=...)` for display — production code never subprocess-executes a fix line; only this test does, under the confinement above. No injection path found: no untrusted-content substitution, no execution outside the fixture cwd. Root-cause history verified clean: `git log --all -p -S<the operator's home-directory literal> -- specs/releases/0.4.7/` and the equivalent `-S` search for a synthetic email literal both return zero commits — no operator-local path or synthetic email literal is reachable from any ref under that tree. Push-gate replay over the full candidate range (`refs/heads/feature/0.4.7 9c4e031c... refs/heads/feature/0.4.7 6cef01f8...` piped to `dadaia ci push-gate-check`) exits 0, denylist-scan banner only, no BLOCKED line. `tests/integration/test_repo_self_scan.py` is green (4 passed) — this run is materially stronger than the prior verdict's baseline: T-047-22 (fix commit e743098d, reviewed as part of this delta's F1-F6 group) deleted the privacy scan's last path-scoped `exclude_regex` carve-out and its `_TESTS_SCOPE_BASELINE` tolerated-pairs list entirely, widening the self-scan to a plain zero-tolerance check over the whole tracked tree (`.github/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` included) with one real operator username removed from fixtures in the same commit — a net reduction in privacy-scan bug surface, not a new risk. No dependency file (`pyproject.toml` dependencies/groups, `poetry.lock`) changed in either the delta or the full 6cef01f8..HEAD range — `pyproject.toml`'s only edits are the version bump to 0.4.7 (already reviewed) and moving the ruff/mypy cache directories to a relative, in-tree-adjacent path (config, not a dependency). No CI workflow, Dockerfile, compose, or Terraform file changed in the delta. `git diff -U0` over the delta against the secret-pattern regex and a private-key-header grep: 0 matches. `dadaia doctor --json`: 12975/12975 canonical, 100%, 0 findings. `candidate.py`'s three `ArchiveError` messages and one `already exists` message changed to the one-fix-line-per-refusal grammar (T-047-14) — wording only, confirmed by diff: still zero `symlink`/`resolve(` occurrences in the file, so the carried-forward LOW finding from the prior verdict is unchanged, not worsened. `schemas.py` is byte-identical across the whole delta. No new HIGH/CRITICAL surface found; nothing in this delta touches an authenticated production endpoint or a live credential. Snapshot, not a guarantee of "secure" (DADAIA.md 7.5) — the operator owns the ship decision.

findings.message: New test seam reviewed for injection: tests/integration/test_doctor_fix_lines_clear_their_finding.py executes real doctor fix lines via bash -c — confirmed safe by construction
findings.detail_md: Every `<placeholder>` substitution value comes from a hardcoded `Plant.substitutions` literal in the test module (no file content, no external input); `_resolve()` asserts no unresolved `<` token survives. Every executed command runs with `cwd=root`, pytest's own `tmp_path` fixture; the shared `_git()` helper additionally restricts `HOME`/`PATH`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`. Production code (`dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/doctor.py`'s `render_fix_help()`) only ever displays a `fix_help` string via `typer.Option(help=...)` and never subprocess-executes it — execution of a fix line happens only inside this test, inside the confinement above. No injection path.

findings.message: T-047-22 removal of the privacy baseline's last path-scoped exclude_regex carve-out (commit e743098d) reduces scan surface, reviewed clean
findings.detail_md: The carve-out existed only to exempt two synthetic fixture literals that had leaked into an unamendable, already-published main squash-commit body. This delta deletes the carve-out, its two dedicated tests, and the entire 23-row `_TESTS_SCOPE_BASELINE` tolerated-pairs list, replacing every incidental test fixture literal with values the baseline already excludes by design (the generic placeholder home path, RFC 5737 `192.0.2.0/24`, `@example.invalid`) or with run-time-composed non-tracked literals (`tests/helpers/privacy_fixtures.py`). `tests/integration/test_repo_self_scan.py` now asserts a plain zero over the whole tracked tree, widened to include `.github/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Verified green (4 passed) on this head. One real operator username was removed from fixtures in the same commit. Net effect: strictly less privacy-scan bug surface than the prior verdict's baseline.
